sources.note: Trains a 1.5B reasoning model to emit one of three mode tokens (NoThink, Short, Long) as the very first token of its response and to reason under that mode's budget, learned end-to-end inside GRPO with no separate router.
sources.title: Learning When to Think: Adaptive Reasoning for Test-Time Compute Allocation

sources.note: ARES trains multimodal reasoning models to spend exploration effort in proportion to problem difficulty, using sliding-window token entropy as the signal for when and how much to explore.
sources.title: ARES: Multimodal Adaptive Reasoning via Difficulty-Aware Token-Level Entropy Shaping

sources.note: DR2Seg splits reasoning segmentation into a description stage and a referring-segmentation stage and rewards the model when a shorter self-contained description still yields the right mask, cutting reasoning length while raising gIoU.
sources.title: DR$^2$Seg: Decomposed Two-Stage Rollouts for Efficient Reasoning Segmentation in Multimodal Large Language Models

sources.note: QuRL runs the rollout phase of RL-with-verifiable-rewards training with an INT8 or FP8 quantized copy of the actor, adding an adaptive clipping range and an invariant weight-scaling trick to keep the low-precision policy from collapsing, for 20-80% faster rollout.
sources.title: QuRL: Low-Precision Reinforcement Learning for Efficient Reasoning

sources.note: GFPO samples a larger group of rollouts per problem during RL training and updates only on the top-k by length or by reward-per-token, converting extra training-time compute into shorter responses at inference.
sources.title: Sample More to Think Less: Group Filtered Policy Optimization for Concise Reasoning

sources.note: ShorterBetter takes the length of the shortest correct response in a sampled group as a per-problem target and rewards the model for matching it, cutting output length by 50%-80% on DeepSeek-Distill-Qwen-1.5B/7B.
sources.title: ShorterBetter: Guiding Reasoning Models to Find Optimal Inference Length for Efficient Reasoning

result.definition: Reinforcement learning in which the reward is a programmatic check of the final answer rather than a learned preference model, and the dominant post-training recipe among the reasoning models this archive tracks. Sources here treat it as the cause of the problem as often as the cure: it applies one maximum response length uniformly to every training sample, which wastes compute on long incorrect traces early and blocks the chains hard problems need later, and one paper argues it functions mainly as an elicitation mechanism, improving pass@k at small k while staying bounded by the base model's latent capability at large k. Its requirement that answers be checkable is also what confines most of this archive's evidence to mathematics, code and multiple-choice science.
